sanskrit: saṃprāpya satkāram atīva tebhyaḥ; provāca kasya prathitāḥ stha saumyāḥ ūcus tatas te 'bhyupagamya sarve; dhanaṃ tavedaṃ vihitaṃ sutasya
english: Having received exceptional honour from them, he asked: 'Whose celebrated ones are you, O gentle ones?' Then all of them approached and said: 'This wealth has been appointed for your son.'

sanskrit: deśe tu deśe tu sa pūjyamānas; tāṃś caiva śṛṇvan madhurān pralāpān praśāntabhūyiṣṭharajāḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ; samāsasādāṅgapatiṃ purastham
english: Honoured in every region, listening to those sweet words, with his passion now largely appeased and his heart gladdened, he approached the lord of Aṅga who stood before him.

sanskrit: saṃpūjitas tena nararṣabheṇa; dadarśa putraṃ divi devaṃ yathendram śāntāṃ snuṣāṃ caiva dadarśa tatra; saudāminīm uccarantīṃ yathaiva
english: Duly honoured by that bull among men, he saw his son radiant as a god in heaven like Indra; and there too he saw his daughter-in-law Śānta, rising up like a flash of lightning.

sanskrit: grāmāṃś ca ghoṣāṃś ca sutaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā; śāntāṃ ca śānto 'sya paraḥ sa kopaḥ cakāra tasmai paramaṃ prasādaṃ; vibhāṇḍako bhūmipater narendra
english: Having seen the villages, the settlements, his son, and Śānta, his great anger was pacified; Vibhāṇḍaka bestowed his highest blessing on that lord of the earth, O king of kings.

sanskrit: sa tatra nikṣipya sutaṃ maharṣir; uvāca sūryāgnisamaprabhāvam jāte putre vanam evāvrajethā; rājñaḥ priyāṇy asya sarvāṇi kṛtvā
english: There the great seer, having entrusted his son of solar and fiery brilliance, spoke: 'When a son is born, you should return to the forest, having done all that is pleasing to this king.'

sanskrit: sa tadvacaḥ kṛtavān ṛśyaśṛṅgo; yayau ca yatrāsya pitā babhūva śāntā cainaṃ paryacarad yathāvat; khe rohiṇī somam ivānukūlā
english: Ṛśyaśṛṅga did as his father instructed and went to where his father had been; and Śānta attended upon him faithfully, as Rohiṇī in the sky attends upon the moon in harmony.

sanskrit: arundhatī vā subhagā vasiṣṭhaṃ; lopāmudrā vāpi yathā hy agastyam nalasya vā damayantī yathābhūd; yathā śacī vajradharasya caiva
english: As the blessed Arundhatī served Vasiṣṭha, or as Lopāmudrā served Agastya, or as Damayantī was to Nala, or as Śacī to the wielder of the thunderbolt—

sanskrit: nāḍāyanī cendrasenā yathaiva; vaśyā nityaṃ mudgalasyājamīḍha tathā śāntā ṛśyaśṛṅgaṃ vanasthaṃ; prītyā yuktā paryacaran narendra
english: And as Nadayani Indrasenā was ever devoted to Mudgala, O descendant of Ajamīḍha — so Śānta, filled with love, waited upon Ṛśyaśṛṅga dwelling in the forest, O king.

sanskrit: tasyāśramaḥ puṇya eṣo vibhāti; mahāhradaṃ śobhayan puṇyakīrteḥ atra snātaḥ kṛtakṛtyo viśuddhas; tīrthāny anyāny anusaṃyāhi rājan
english: This holy hermitage of his, renowned for its sanctity, shines forth, adorning the great lake. Having bathed here, with all duties fulfilled and purified, go on, O king, to visit the other sacred tirthas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ prayātaḥ kauśikyāḥ pāṇḍavo janamejaya ānupūrvyeṇa sarvāṇi jagāmāyatanāny uta
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the Pāṇḍava departed from the Kauśikī, O Janamejaya, and visited all the sacred shrines in due order.

sanskrit: sa sāgaraṃ samāsādya gaṅgāyāḥ saṃgame nṛpa nadīśatānāṃ pañcānāṃ madhye cakre samāplavam
english: Reaching the ocean at the confluence of the Gaṅgā, O king, he bathed together with hundreds of rivers at the meeting of five streams.

sanskrit: tataḥ samudratīreṇa jagāma vasudhādhipaḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito vīraḥ kaliṅgān prati bhārata
english: Then along the seashore that lord of the earth, the hero, accompanied by his brothers, proceeded toward the Kaliṅgas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca ete kaliṅgāḥ kaunteya yatra vaitaraṇī nadī yatrāyajata dharmo 'pi devāñ śaraṇam etya vai
english: Lomaśa said: These are the Kaliṅgas, O son of Kuntī, where the river Vaitaraṇī flows — where even Dharma himself sought refuge with the gods and performed sacrifice.

sanskrit: ṛṣibhiḥ samupāyuktaṃ yajñiyaṃ giriśobhitam uttaraṃ tīram etad dhi satataṃ dvijasevitam
english: This northern bank, adorned with mountains, consecrated for sacrifice, enriched by sages, is always frequented by the twice-born.

sanskrit: samena devayānena pathā svargam upeyuṣaḥ atra vai ṛṣayo 'nye 'pi purā kratubhir ījire
english: Those who have attained heaven by the straight Devayāna path — here too other sages in former times performed sacrifices with great rites.

sanskrit: atraiva rudro rājendra paśum ādattavān makhe rudraḥ paśuṃ mānavendra bhāgo 'yam iti cābravīt
english: Right here, O king of kings, Rudra seized the sacrificial animal at the sacrifice; Rudra said, O lord of men: 'This is my share.'

sanskrit: hṛte paśau tadā devās tam ūcur bharatarṣabha mā parasvam abhidrogdhā mā dharmān sakalānn aśīḥ
english: When the animal was taken, the gods then said to him, O bull of the Bhāratas: 'Do not seize what belongs to another; do not transgress all the laws of dharma.'

sanskrit: tataḥ kalyāṇarūpābhir vāgbhis te rudram astuvan iṣṭyā cainaṃ tarpayitvā mānayāṃ cakrire tadā
english: Then with words of auspicious form they praised Rudra, and having propitiated him with offerings they then honoured him.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa paśum utsṛjya devayānena jagmivān atrānuvaṃśo rudrasya taṃ nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: Then he released the animal and departed by the Devayāna path. Hear now the lineage of Rudra that is associated with this place, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: ayātayāmaṃ sarvebhyo bhāgebhyo bhāgam uttamam devāḥ saṃkalpayām āsur bhayād rudrasya śāśvatam
english: Out of fear of Rudra, the gods forever resolved that the choicest, freshest share — the best of all portions — would always belong to him.

sanskrit: imāṃ gāthām atra gāyann apaḥ spṛśati yo naraḥ devayānas tasya panthāś cakṣuś caiva prakāśate
english: Whoever sings this hymn here and touches the waters — the Devayāna path and his eyes shall become illumined for him.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vaitaraṇīṃ sarve pāṇḍavā draupadī tathā avatīrya mahābhāgā tarpayāṃ cakrire pitṝn
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then all the Pāṇḍavas, and Draupadī of great fortune, descended into the Vaitaraṇī and made offerings to the ancestors.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca upaspṛśyaiva bhagavann asyāṃ nadyāṃ tapodhana mānuṣād asmi viṣayād apetaḥ paśya lomaśa
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Having touched the waters of this river, O blessed one, O treasure of austerity, I feel as though I have passed beyond the human realm — behold, O Lomaśa.

sanskrit: sarvāṃl lokān prapaśyāmi prasādāt tava suvrata vaikhānasānāṃ japatām eṣa śabdo mahātmanām
english: By your grace, O one of good vows, I behold all the worlds; this is the sound of the great-souled Vaikhānasa sages engaged in recitation.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca triśataṃ vai sahasrāṇi yojanānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira yatra dhvaniṃ śṛṇoṣy enaṃ tūṣṇīm āssva viśāṃ pate
english: Lomaśa said: Three hundred thousand yojanas distant is the place where you hear that sound, O Yudhiṣṭhira — be silent, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: etat svayaṃbhuvo rājan vanaṃ ramyaṃ prakāśate yatrāyajata kaunteya viśvakarmā pratāpavān
english: This, O king, is the delightful forest of Svayambhū that shines forth, where the mighty Viśvakarman performed his sacrifice, O son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: yasmin yajñe hi bhūr dattā kaśyapāya mahātmane saparvatavanoddeśā dakṣiṇā vai svayaṃbhuvā
english: At that sacrifice, the entire earth — with its mountains and forests — was given by Svayambhū as the sacrificial fee to the great-souled Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: avāsīdac ca kaunteya dattamātrā mahī tadā uvāca cāpi kupitā lokeśvaram idaṃ prabhum
english: And no sooner was the earth given than it sank down, O son of Kuntī; and it spoke in anger to that lord of the worlds, its master.

sanskrit: na māṃ martyāya bhagavan kasmai cid dātum arhasi pradānaṃ mogham etat te yāsyāmy eṣā rasātalam
english: 'O blessed one, you ought not give me to any mortal; this gift of yours is in vain — I shall sink into the nether world.'

sanskrit: viṣīdantīṃ tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kaśyapo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ prasādayāṃ babhūvātha tato bhūmiṃ viśāṃ pate
english: Seeing her despondent, the blessed sage Kaśyapa then began to appease the earth, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: tataḥ prasannā pṛthivī tapasā tasya pāṇḍava punar unmajjya salilād vedīrūpā sthitā babhau
english: Then the earth, appeased by his austerity, O Pāṇḍava, rose up again from the waters and stood shining in the form of an altar.

sanskrit: saiṣā prakāśate rājan vedī saṃsthānalakṣaṇā āruhyātra mahārāja vīryavān vai bhaviṣyasi
english: This is that altar shining here, O king, marked by its distinctive form; ascend it, O great king, and you shall become mighty.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca te svastyayanaṃ prayokṣye; yathā tvam enām adhirokṣyase 'dya spṛṣṭā hi martyena tataḥ samudram; eṣā vedī praviśaty ājamīḍha
english: And I shall perform a benedictory rite for you, so that you may ascend it today; for once touched by a mortal, this altar sinks into the ocean, O descendant of Ajamīḍha.

sanskrit: agnir mitro yonir āpo 'tha devyo; viṣṇo retas tvam amṛtasya nābhiḥ evaṃ bruvan pāṇḍava satyavākyaṃ; vedīm imāṃ tvaṃ tarasādhiroha
english: Speaking these true words, O Pāṇḍava: 'You are Agni, you are Mitra, you are the womb, you are the divine waters, you are the seed of Viṣṇu, you are the navel of immortality' — swiftly ascend this altar.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ kṛtasvastyayano mahātmā; yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sāgaragām agacchat kṛtvā ca tacchāsanam asya sarvaṃ; mahendram āsādya niśām uvāsa
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the great-souled Yudhiṣṭhira, the benediction performed, proceeded to the ocean; and having done all that Lomaśa commanded, he reached Mahendra and spent the night there.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa tatra tām uṣitvaikāṃ rajanīṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ tāpasānāṃ paraṃ cakre satkāraṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spent that one night there, the lord of the earth offered the highest honour to the ascetics together with his brothers.

sanskrit: lomaśaś cāsya tān sarvān ācakhyau tatra tāpasān bhṛgūn aṅgirasaś caiva vāsiṣṭhān atha kāśyapān
english: And Lomaśa introduced to him all those ascetics there — the Bhṛgus, the Aṅgirases, the Vasishthyas, and the Kashyapas.

sanskrit: tān sametya sa rājarṣir abhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ rāmasyānucaraṃ vīram apṛcchad akṛtavraṇam
english: Meeting them, that royal seer paid his respects with joined palms and then asked Akṛtavraṇa, the heroic companion of Rāma.

sanskrit: kadā nu rāmo bhagavāṃs tāpasān darśayiṣyati tenaivāhaṃ prasaṅgena draṣṭum icchāmi bhārgavam
english: 'When will the blessed Rāma show himself to the ascetics? On that very occasion I wish to behold the descendant of Bhṛgu.'

sanskrit: akṛtavraṇa uvāca āyān evāsi vidito rāmasya viditātmanaḥ prītis tvayi ca rāmasya kṣipraṃ tvāṃ darśayiṣyati
english: Akṛtavraṇa said: Your coming is already known to Rāma, who knows all souls; and Rāma's affection for you is such that he will show himself to you soon.

sanskrit: caturdaśīm aṣṭamīṃ ca rāmaṃ paśyanti tāpasāḥ asyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ bhavitrī ca caturdaśī
english: The ascetics see Rāma on the fourteenth and the eighth lunar days; when this night has passed, the fourteenth will arrive.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhavān anugato vīraṃ jāmadagnyaṃ mahābalam pratyakṣadarśī sarvasya pūrvavṛttasya karmaṇaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: You have accompanied that hero, the son of Jamadagni, of great might, and are an eyewitness to all his past deeds.

sanskrit: sa bhavān kathayatv etad yathā rāmeṇa nirjitāḥ āhave kṣatriyāḥ sarve kathaṃ kena ca hetunā
english: Let you therefore tell us how Rāma conquered all the kshatriyas in battle, and by what means and for what reason.

sanskrit: akṛtavraṇa uvāca kanyakubje mahān āsīt pārthivaḥ sumahābalaḥ gādhīti viśruto loke vanavāsaṃ jagāma saḥ
english: Akṛtavraṇa said: In Kānyakubja there was a great and exceedingly mighty king, renowned in the world as Gādhi; he went to live in the forest.

sanskrit: vane tu tasya vasataḥ kanyā jajñe 'psaraḥsamā ṛcīko bhārgavas tāṃ ca varayām āsa bhārata
english: While he lived in the forest, a daughter was born to him who was like an apsara; the Bhārgava Ṛcīka sought her in marriage, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato rājā brāhmaṇaṃ saṃśitavratam ucitaṃ naḥ kule kiṃ cit pūrvair yat saṃpravartitam
english: Then the king said to that brahmin of rigorous vows: 'There is something customary in our family, established by our ancestors—'

sanskrit: ekataḥ śyāmakarṇānāṃ pāṇḍurāṇāṃ tarasvinām sahasraṃ vājināṃ śulkam iti viddhi dvijottama
english: 'Know this as the bride-price, O best of twice-born: a thousand swift white horses, each with one black ear.'

sanskrit: na cāpi bhagavān vācyo dīyatām iti bhārgava deyā me duhitā ceyaṃ tvadvidhāya mahātmane
english: 'And do not say, O blessed Bhārgava, that the price should be waived — my daughter is to be given to a great soul such as you.'

sanskrit: ṛcīka uvāca ekataḥśyāmakarṇānāṃ pāṇḍurāṇāṃ tarasvinām dāsyāmy aśvasahasraṃ te mama bhāryā sutāstu te
english: Ṛcīka said: I will give you a thousand swift white horses, each with one black ear; let your daughter be my wife and your son-in-law be me.

sanskrit: akṛtavraṇa uvāca sa tatheti pratijñāya rājan varuṇam abravīt ekataḥśyāmakarṇānāṃ pāṇḍurāṇāṃ tarasvinām sahasraṃ vājinām ekaṃ śulkārthaṃ me pradīyatām
english: Akṛtavraṇa said: Having agreed to this, O king, he addressed Varuṇa: 'For the bride-price, let a thousand swift white horses, each with one black ear, be given to me.'

sanskrit: tasmai prādāt sahasraṃ vai vājināṃ varuṇas tadā tad aśvatīrthaṃ vikhyātam utthitā yatra te hayāḥ
english: Varuṇa gave him a thousand horses at that time; that place is known as Aśvatīrtha, where those horses emerged.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyāṃ kanyakubje vai dadau satyavatīṃ tadā tato gādhiḥ sutāṃ tasmai janyāś cāsan surās tadā labdhvā hayasahasraṃ tu tāṃś ca dṛṣṭvā divaukasaḥ
english: At Kānyakubja on the Gaṅgā, Gādhi then gave his daughter Satyavatī to him; and upon receiving the thousand horses and seeing them, the gods dwellers in heaven rejoiced.

sanskrit: dharmeṇa labdhvā tāṃ bhāryām ṛcīko dvijasattamaḥ yathākāmaṃ yathājoṣaṃ tayā reme sumadhyayā
english: Having won her as his wife by righteous means, Ṛcīka, the best of twice-born, sported with that slender-waisted one to his heart's content and delight.

sanskrit: taṃ vivāhe kṛte rājan sabhāryam avalokakaḥ ājagāma bhṛguśreṣṭhaḥ putraṃ dṛṣṭvā nananda ca
english: After the marriage was performed, O king, the foremost of the Bhṛgus came to look upon his son together with his wife, and upon seeing him was filled with joy.

sanskrit: bhāryāpatī tam āsīnaṃ guruṃ suragaṇārcitam arcitvā paryupāsīnau prāñjalī tasthatus tadā
english: The husband and wife, honouring that teacher who was worshipped even by the host of gods, stood attending him on either side with joined palms.

sanskrit: tataḥ snuṣāṃ sa bhagavān prahṛṣṭo bhṛgur abravīt varaṃ vṛṇīṣva subhage dātā hy asmi tavepsitam
english: Then the blessed Bhṛgu, delighted, said to his daughter-in-law: 'Choose a boon, O fortunate one, for I am here to grant what you desire.'

sanskrit: sā vai prasādayām āsa taṃ guruṃ putrakāraṇāt ātmanaś caiva mātuś ca prasādaṃ ca cakāra saḥ
english: She then propitiated that teacher for the sake of children — both for herself and for her mother; and he granted his grace to both.

sanskrit: bhṛgur uvāca ṛtau tvaṃ caiva mātā ca snāte puṃsavanāya vai āliṅgetāṃ pṛthag vṛkṣau sāśvatthaṃ tvam udumbaram
english: Bhṛgu said: 'At the proper season, you and your mother, having bathed with the rite of pumsavana for a male child, must each embrace a different tree — you the udumbara, and the ashvattha.'

sanskrit: āliṅgane tu te rājaṃś cakratuḥ sma viparyayam kadā cid bhṛgur āgacchat taṃ ca veda viparyayam
english: But the two of them, O king, exchanged the trees in their embrace; and when Bhṛgu came by, he discerned the exchange.

sanskrit: athovāca mahātejā bhṛguḥ satyavatīṃ snuṣām brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatravṛttir vai tava putro bhaviṣyati
english: Then the greatly splendid Bhṛgu said to his daughter-in-law Satyavatī: 'Your son will be a brahmin who follows the conduct of a kshatriya.'

sanskrit: kṣatriyo brāhmaṇācāro mātus tava suto mahān bhaviṣyati mahāvīryaḥ sādhūnāṃ mārgam āsthitaḥ
english: 'And your mother's great son will be a kshatriya who follows brahminical conduct — of great valour and treading the path of the righteous.'

sanskrit: tataḥ prasādayām āsa śvaśuraṃ sā punaḥ punaḥ na me putro bhaved īdṛk kāmaṃ pautro bhaved iti
english: Then she repeatedly propitiated her father-in-law, saying: 'Let not my son be such — let my grandson be so instead, if you will.'

sanskrit: evam astv iti sā tena pāṇḍava pratinanditā jamadagniṃ tataḥ putraṃ sā jajñe kāla āgate tejasā varcasā caiva yuktaṃ bhārgavanandanam
english: 'So be it,' said he; she was thus granted her wish, O Pāṇḍava; and in time she gave birth to her son Jamadagni, the delight of the Bhṛgus, endowed with brilliance and radiance.

sanskrit: sa vardhamānas tejasvī vedasyādhyayanena vai bahūn ṛṣīn mahātejāḥ pāṇḍaveyātyavartata
english: Growing up, that splendid one, of great brilliance, surpassed many sages through his study of the Vedas, O descendant of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: taṃ tu kṛtsno dhanurvedaḥ pratyabhād bharatarṣabha caturvidhāni cāstrāṇi bhāskaropamavarcasam
english: The entire science of archery, along with the fourfold knowledge of weapons, became manifest to him, O bull of the Bhāratas, whose radiance was like the sun.

sanskrit: akṛtavraṇa uvāca sa vedādhyayane yukto jamadagnir mahātapāḥ tapas tepe tato devān niyamād vaśam ānayat
english: Akṛtavraṇa said: Jamadagni, of great austerity, devoted to Vedic study, performed tapas and thereby brought the gods under his control by his discipline.

sanskrit: sa prasenajitaṃ rājann adhigamya narādhipam reṇukāṃ varayām āsa sa ca tasmai dadau nṛpaḥ
english: Approaching king Prasenajit, O king, lord of men, he sought Reṇukā in marriage; and the king gave her to him.

sanskrit: reṇukāṃ tv atha saṃprāpya bhāryāṃ bhārgavanandanaḥ āśramasthas tayā sārdhaṃ tapas tepe 'nukūlayā
english: Having thus obtained Reṇukā as his wife, the delight of the Bhṛgus lived in the hermitage and performed austerities together with her, who was devoted and compliant.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ kumārāś catvāro jajñire rāmapañcamāḥ sarveṣām ajaghanyas tu rāma āsīj jaghanyajaḥ
english: Four sons were born to her, Rāma being the fifth; Rāma, the last-born, was the youngest of them all.

sanskrit: phalāhāreṣu sarveṣu gateṣv atha suteṣu vai reṇukā snātum agamat kadā cin niyatavratā
english: One day, all the sons having gone out to gather fruits, Reṇukā, steadfast in her vows, went to bathe.

sanskrit: sā tu citrarathaṃ nāma mārttikāvatakaṃ nṛpam dadarśa reṇukā rājann āgacchantī yadṛcchayā
english: And Reṇukā, as she was going along, happened by chance to see a king named Citraratha, the lord of Martikavata, O king.

sanskrit: krīḍantaṃ salile dṛṣṭvā sabhāryaṃ padmamālinam ṛddhimantaṃ tatas tasya spṛhayām āsa reṇukā
english: Seeing him sporting in the water with his wife, garlanded with lotuses, in the full flush of his prosperity, Reṇukā was filled with longing for him.

sanskrit: vyabhicārāt tu sā tasmāt klinnāmbhasi vicetanā praviveśāśramaṃ trastā tāṃ vai bhartānvabudhyata
english: On account of that transgression in her mind, she came back trembling and distraught, her clothes still wet from the water, and entered the hermitage; her husband perceived it in her.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā cyutāṃ dhairyād brāhmyā lakṣmyā vivarjitām dhikśabdena mahātejā garhayām āsa vīryavān
english: Seeing her fallen from her steadfastness and stripped of her brahminical radiance, the greatly splendid and valiant one censured her with words of reproach.

sanskrit: tato jyeṣṭho jāmadagnyo rumaṇvān nāma nāmataḥ ājagāma suṣeṇaś ca vasur viśvāvasus tathā
english: Then the eldest son of Jamadagni named Rumanvan arrived, and Suṣeṇa, and Vasu, and Viśvāvasu as well.

sanskrit: tān ānupūrvyād bhagavān vadhe mātur acodayat na ca te jātasaṃmohāḥ kiṃ cid ūcur vicetasaḥ
english: The blessed one urged them each in turn to kill their mother; but they, overcome with confusion, said nothing, standing senseless.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaśāpa tān kopāt te śaptāś cetanāṃ jahuḥ mṛgapakṣisadharmāṇaḥ kṣipram āsañ jaḍopamāḥ
english: Then in anger he cursed them; cursed, they lost their consciousness and quickly became like inert beings, taking on the nature of animals and birds.

sanskrit: tato rāmo 'bhyagāt paścād āśramaṃ paravīrahā tam uvāca mahāmanyur jamadagnir mahātapāḥ
english: Then Rāma, the slayer of enemy heroes, came to the hermitage afterward; and Jamadagni, greatly wrathful and of great austerity, said to him—

sanskrit: jahīmāṃ mātaraṃ pāpāṃ mā ca putra vyathāṃ kṛthāḥ tata ādāya paraśuṃ rāmo mātuḥ śiro 'harat
english: 'Kill this sinful mother, and let not grief afflict you, my son.' Then taking up the axe, Rāma struck off his mother's head.

sanskrit: tatas tasya mahārāja jamadagner mahātmanaḥ kopo agacchat sahasā prasannaś cābravīd idam
english: Then, O great king, the anger of the great-souled Jamadagni suddenly departed; and, now pleased, he spoke these words.
